You’ve heard of SWE-Bench, Terminal-Bench and ARC-AGI. But I bet you’ve never heard of one that tests how far AI can take a total noob in game dev.

Welcome to NoobBench. https://t.co/PZXDFofS0l

Created a "benchmark benchmark": a frequency distribution of which benchmarks were reported by the frontier labs in 2026: https://t.co/3Psnma9OOh

Some observations:
- HLE, SWE-Bench Pro, DeepSWE, and Terminal-Bench saw universal adoption
- Scale AI is behind two of those four https://t.co/UuYw6nzTBw

AI term of the day: Benchmark

A benchmark is a standard test used to compare AI models. Every time a new model launches, you'll see charts showing it scored higher than the others on tests with names like MMLU, GSM8K or SWE-bench.

Each benchmark checks a different skill. MMLU https://t.co/W5U4NGf54g

Jason Wei published a benchmark benchmark: which benchmarks frontier labs actually reported in 2026. HLE, SWE-Bench Pro, DeepSWE and Terminal-Bench saw universal adoption. DeepSWE went from first release in June to all 12 labs. Terminal-Bench cycled four versions in one year.

Benchmark saturation may be a measurement problem.

Re-scoring 8 agent benchmarks: top-10 neighbours on SWE-bench Verified differ by less than the tests' own errors. On Terminal-Bench, pass/fail-tied models differ 10x+ on what tests discard.

Grading with one bit?

Cognition says its SWE-2 Flash went from 0.9% to 20.0% on Terminal-Bench 4.0 after a mid-training stage.

Real gain or benchmark polish?

A new open-source benchmark, Parsimony, measures how much extra code AI models and agent harnesses add versus human fixes, counting syntax units not lines. The median model adds 1.9× the human fix on SWE-bench Verified but about 1× on DeepSWE. Harness results for…

GPT-5.1's best feature isn't a benchmark — it stops overthinking easy tasks. A simple npm question: 2s, 50 tokens vs 10s, 250 for GPT-5. Plus a 'none' reasoning mode, now the API default. SWE-bench 76.3% vs 72.8%, same price. Will no-reasoning be your agents' new default?

Agent benchmarks aren't running out of tasks. 

They're running out of grading. Most reduce a run to a single pass/fail bit. 

On SWE-bench Verified, agents next to each other in the top ten differ by less than the tests' own error.
